# AMD Instinct validation campaign for vLLM serving (functional and performance parity)

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's core unknown: whether vLLM serving on AMD
Instinct accelerators (ROCm) reaches functional and performance parity with
the platform's CUDA-based builds for the supported model set. It runs a
validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware and produces a
per-model report with a go/no-go recommendation that defines the scope of the
serving-runtime productization work. The platform currently ships only CUDA
runtime builds and has no first-hand parity data for its supported model set.

## Scope

- Define the validation campaign plan: the supported model set to be covered,
  functional pass/fail criteria per model, and performance parity metrics and
  baselines measured against the platform's CUDA vLLM runtime builds.
- Execute functional validation: serve each model in the supported set with
  upstream vLLM ROCm builds on AMD Instinct nodes and record results
  (correctness, failures, workarounds found).
- Execute performance validation: collect throughput and latency parity data
  per model against the CUDA baseline.
- Produce a validation report stating, per model: functional result,
  performance parity result, blockers encountered (driver level, ROCm level,
  upstream vLLM level), and a go/no-go recommendation for productization.
- Securing access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (procurement or partner-lab
  access) is part of this epic's work where the team can drive it; the access
  itself is an externally granted precondition (see Risks).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation plan exists that enumerates every model in the supported model
  set with explicit functional pass/fail criteria and defined performance
  parity metrics and CUDA baselines.
- The campaign's validated report exists and covers every model in the plan,
  stating per-model functional results, performance parity data, and blockers.
- The report states a go/no-go recommendation per model that jointly define
  the productization scope for the supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime.
- Any driver or ROCm-level prerequisites discovered by the campaign are
  documented with the versions used.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishing functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
  supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks / Notes

- **Hardware access is unresolved and externally controlled** (procurement or
  partner-lab). No AMD Instinct nodes exist in the CI fleet today. The access
  being granted is not something this epic's deliverable produces; if access
  cannot be secured, the campaign — and the rest of the strategy gated on its
  outcome — stalls. Escalate early at the program level.
- Upstream ROCm image cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities; pin the versions validated so results are reproducible.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

This epic delivers a supported, productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the
models cleared by the validation campaign — the platform's first shipped and
supported AMD GPU serving capability. Today the platform productizes only
CUDA (NVIDIA) vLLM runtime builds; ROCm builds exist upstream but are not
shipped or supported. The work builds on the existing vLLM runtime
productization path (midstream repo, per-platform image releases, ServingRuntime
integration) and adds the ROCm variant alongside the CUDA builds.

## Scope

- Build and release vLLM ROCm runtime images from the midstream vLLM repo for
  the platform version, based on the upstream ROCm builds and the versions
  pinned during validation.
- Define and ship the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime resource(s) that
  expose the ROCm vLLM runtime to users, restricted to the model set cleared
  by the validation campaign.
- Verify the runtime works end-to-end under KServe: InferenceServices using
  the ROCm runtime deploy and serve on AMD Instinct nodes (serverless and/or
  raw deployment mode as supported), with Ready predictor status and
  OpenAI-compatible endpoints responding. KServe itself requires no code
  changes — this is a compatibility validation of the device-agnostic serving
  stack, owned by the same team.
- Ensure the ROCm runtime coexists with the existing CUDA vLLM runtime builds
  without regression to the CUDA serving path.
- Document the support scope (cleared model list, driver prerequisites) as
  engineering input to the user-facing documentation effort.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A vLLM ROCm runtime image is built and released through the platform's
  standard runtime image process for the target platform version.
- A ServingRuntime exposing the ROCm vLLM runtime is shipped, and the models
  it supports match the go/no-go scope produced by the validation campaign.
- KServe InferenceServices using the ROCm runtime successfully deploy and
  serve inference requests on AMD Instinct nodes, with predictor Ready status
  and responding OpenAI-compatible endpoints, for every model in the cleared
  scope.
- Serving the existing CUDA vLLM runtime builds shows no regression (existing
  runtime behavior and endpoints unchanged).
- The cleared model list and driver prerequisites are handed off as validated
  engineering input for the documentation deliverable.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks / Notes

- Scope is gated on the validation campaign's go/no-go outcome: if only a
  subset of models clears, the runtime is productized for that subset; a full
  no-go removes this epic's productization work in favor of documenting
  results.
- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities; sustained alignment with our release trains is an ongoing
  maintenance risk beyond initial productization.

# PyTorch training on ROCm for single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs

## Description

This epic enables PyTorch training on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) for the
platform's Training Operator: PyTorchJob workloads using ROCm-enabled PyTorch
run in single-GPU and multi-GPU topologies on AMD GPU nodes. Upstream PyTorch
publishes ROCm support; this epic brings that support into the platform's
supported training path. The Training Operator itself (PyTorchJob CRD, job
topology, pod creation) is unchanged in its scheduling behavior — the work is
the ROCm-enabled training runtime and its validation.

## Scope

- Provide or productize ROCm-enabled PyTorch training runtime images usable
  by PyTorchJob worker and launcher containers, pinned to upstream ROCm/PyTorch
  versions validated during the work.
- Validate single-GPU PyTorchJobs on AMD Instinct nodes: jobs run to
  completion with functional training results.
- Validate multi-GPU (and, where in scope, multi-node) PyTorchJob topologies
  on AMD Instinct nodes, including distributed training initialization across
  AMD GPUs.
- Validate that PyTorchJobs on AMD nodes are admitted through Kueue when
  workload queueing is enabled, with amd.com/gpu resources accounted under
  the queue quota (end-to-end admission check shared with the queueing-layer
  quota work, which proceeds in parallel).
- Document any AMD driver or ROCm-level prerequisites discovered, as
  engineering input to the user-facing documentation effort.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A ROCm-enabled PyTorch training runtime image is available and usable in
  PyTorchJob worker specifications.
- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using the ROCm runtime runs to completion on AMD
  Instinct nodes with correct training results.
- A multi-GPU PyTorchJob using the ROCm runtime runs to completion on AMD
  Instinct nodes with distributed training functioning across GPUs.
- With workload queueing enabled, PyTorchJobs requesting amd.com/gpu are
  admitted through Kueue and the quota is enforced (jobs wait when quota is
  exhausted, run when admitted).
- Driver/ROCm prerequisites and validated configurations are handed off as
  engineering input for the documentation deliverable.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling
  (runtime/job side; quota handling in the queueing layer is covered by the
  parallel queueing-layer work).

## Risks / Notes

- Validation requires physical AMD Instinct hardware — the same
  externally-controlled access risk as the serving validation campaign; none
  exists in the CI fleet today. Secure access through the same procurement or
  partner-lab channel.
- Upstream PyTorch/ROCm image cadence is controlled upstream; pin validated
  versions.

# Kueue admission and amd.com/gpu quota handling for ROCm training jobs

## Description

This epic makes the platform's queueing layer (Kueue, the Distributed
Workloads stack) correctly handle AMD GPU resources: accelerated jobs that
request `amd.com/gpu` are admitted through ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota with
the platform's established admission semantics, so ROCm training jobs queue
and run under quota like their NVIDIA counterparts. Kueue's quota model is
resource-agnostic, but the platform's GPU resource discovery and queue
configuration today are built around the NVIDIA GPU Operator; this epic
covers the AMD side of admission and quota.

## Scope

- Define and support queue configuration (resource flavors, ClusterQueue /
  LocalQueue coverage) that accounts for `amd.com/gpu` resources, matching the
  quota model already used for NVIDIA GPUs.
- Validate admission semantics for jobs requesting `amd.com/gpu`: all-or-nothing
  (gang) admission via waitForPodsReady for multi-GPU/multi-pod jobs, queuing
  when quota is exhausted, and admission when quota is available.
- Validate that PyTorchJobs on AMD GPU nodes are admitted through the Kueue
  integration with `amd.com/gpu` accounted under quota (end-to-end check
  shared with the training-runtime work, which proceeds in parallel).
- Cover single-GPU and multi-GPU job shapes in validation.
- Document required queue configuration for AMD GPU quotas as engineering
  input to the user-facing documentation effort.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Queue configuration exists that accounts for `amd.com/gpu` under
  ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota, consistent with the platform's existing GPU
  quota model.
- A job requesting `amd.com/gpu` within quota is admitted; a job exceeding
  available quota waits in the queue and is admitted when quota frees up.
- A multi-pod job requesting `amd.com/gpu` is admitted all-or-nothing
  (waitForPodsReady gang semantics hold).
- PyTorchJobs requesting `amd.com/gpu` are admitted through the Kueue
  integration end-to-end on AMD GPU nodes.
- Required queue configuration for AMD GPU quotas is handed off as
  engineering input for the documentation deliverable.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling
  (queueing/quota side; the PyTorchJob runtime side is covered by the parallel
  training-runtime work).

## Risks / Notes

- End-to-end validation requires physical AMD Instinct hardware — the same
  externally-controlled access risk as the rest of the strategy.
- GPU resource discovery for AMD nodes depends on the accelerator discovery
  mechanism exposing `amd.com/gpu` (the platform's current discovery
  dependency is the NVIDIA GPU Operator); confirm the AMD equivalent during
  validation.

the validated model list for vLLM serving on ROCm, plus the supported PyTorch
training path with its Kueue quota configuration. It runs after the
implementation work so the docs describe what was actually built and
validated.

## Scope

- Supported AMD Instinct hardware for RHOAI serving and training.
- Driver and ROCm-level prerequisites for AMD GPU nodes, including required
  versions as validated during the campaign and implementation work.
- The validated model list for vLLM ROCm serving (the go/no-go scope produced

- Published documentation describes the supported PyTorch training path on
